paragraphs: Children in care in Conwy are looked after by Foster Wales Conwy, the fostering service of Conwy County Borough Council, and by the services shown above. It is part of Foster Wales, the network of council fostering services across Wales, and like every council in Wales it has signed up to the National Commitment on the support foster carers receive.

Foster Wales Conwy publishes what it pays. It describes a child's allowance of £204 to £255 a week, depending on the child's age, and an enhanced fee of £250.08, with further payments for birthdays, holidays, festivals and mileage and an emergency grant when needed. Full-time carers who have no child living with them keep receiving the fee. The council does not give a year for these figures, so ask for the current rates when you enquire.

There is more besides money. The council lists free use of its FFit Conwy leisure centres for the whole household, a parking permit for every council car park, up to 100% council tax relief for full-time carers, membership of The Fostering Network and Cadw, a reimbursed Blue Light Card, a free Max Card, and five days' special leave for council staff who foster. Support is available around the clock, a clinical psychologist works with the team, and there are groups for carers of babies and toddlers and for men who foster. The council says people from the LGBTQ+ community are welcome to foster with it.

See our North Wales, Gwynedd and Flintshire pages for neighbouring areas, then talk to Foster Wales Conwy and one or two of the services above, and compare training, support and pay before you choose.
